title: Airgapped release signal procedures and artifact verification - draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an operational playbook for releases to private/Airgapped deployments where normal internet access is restricted and GitOps (Argo) + Helm + signed artifacts are the primary delivery mechanism. It focuses on the signal design (what to observe), artifact verification steps (image + SBOM + attestation), and Terraform/Helm gating mechanics for a safe upgrade path.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target: on-prem clusters or VPCs with limited egress (customers with airgapped or restricted proxy).
- Delivery model: artifacts (images, charts, SBOMs, attestations) are pushed to an internal registry/airgap bundle, then imported into the customer's artifact mirror prior to promotion.
- CI/CD: central CI builds artifacts and publishes a signed bundle that SRE/Customer ops pulls into their mirror. ArgoCD in the target environment reconciles local repo state.
- We assume cosign/notation-based signing and an attestation store (could be in-repo or OCI).

High-level signal model (what success/failure looks like):
- Preflight success (PASS): all preflight checks (chart lint, schema validation, image signature, attestation existence, SBOM checksum) return PASS.
- Canary health (WARN/ERROR thresholds): during canary rollout monitor the following signals with thresholds: 5xx rate >0.5% over 5m OR 95th latency increase > 2x baseline OR error % on critical RPCs > 1% -> escalate to rollforward hold.
- Data-loss guardrails: migrations must be reversible OR flagged with manual approval if irreversible.
- Auto-rollback triggers: crashlooping pods > N within 2m, persistent volume attach failures, control-plane reconciliation stuck > 10m.

Pre-release checklist (artifact & infra gating):
1) Build artifacts: image, Helm chart, SBOM, manifest bundle.
   - Ensure image is built from tagged commit and reproducible build pipeline.
   - Generate SBOM (CycloneDX) and include checksum in chart values.
2) Sign artifacts: cosign sign for image digest; create an attestation stating build-id, base-image, provenance, and tests-run.
   - Store signature and attestation in the customer's approved OCI registry or the airgap bundle.
3) Terraform module outputs: the delivery Terraform modules that manage customer's artifact mirror should produce: mirror_artifact_path, mirror_sync_timestamp, and attestation_index. These names must be stable across versions.
   - Note: prefer explicit versioned keys (e.g. mirror_artifact_path_v1) when rolling major changes to avoid drift.
4) Verify SBOM and checksums locally before generating the bundle.
5) Generate Argo application snapshot (manifest repo tag) and attach the signed manifest metadata file to the bundle.

Airgap bundle format (recommended minimal):
- images.tar.gz (OCI images) OR OCI index + registry export format
- charts/<release>-<version>.tgz
- attestations/<image-digest>.att.json
- sbom/<image-digest>.cyclonedx.json
- manifest-snapshot/<repo-tag>.yaml
- signature-index.json (mapping images/charts -> cosign signatures + attestation link)

Transfer & import process (operator steps):
1) Copy bundle into customer mirror staging area.
2) Run local verification script: validate-signatures --bundle ./bundle --trust-roots /etc/redwood/trust-roots
   - Script checks: cosign verify for each image digest, attestation present, sbom checksum matches, chart provenance.
3) If verification PASS, import to registry and update mirror git repo to point to new manifest-snapshot tag.
4) Wait for ArgoCD to detect new tag. If Argo is in offline mode, trigger a local sync job (kubectl apply argocd-offline-sync --namespace argocd).

Argo/Helm promotion pattern (recommended):
- Do not push new chart versions directly to production branch. Use a three-stage branch model: staging -> canary -> prod. Each stage corresponds to an Argo ApplicationSet instance with different values overlays.
- Automated promotion flow: when staging apps healthy for 10m AND canary thresholds are met, a CI step creates a PR to the canary branch with the manifest-snapshot tag and signature metadata. This PR requires at least one approver (on-call SRE).

Canary release signal flow (detailed):
1) Deploy 10% of replicas (or single node pool slice) with the new release.
2) Monitor: latency (P50/P95/P99), request error %, CPU/memory OOMs, GC spikes, downstream dependency errors.
3) If any signal crosses WARN threshold -> slow down (pause deployment, request manual review). If ERROR threshold -> rollback by patching Argo manifest to previous image digest (automated revert PR created).
4) After 30m of stable metrics, promote to 50% and repeat checks. Final promote to 100% requires additional approval.

Rollback mechanics and fast path: 
- Preferred rollback is manifest tag revert (Argo sees old tag -> apply previous config). However, in airgapped environments manual override may be faster:
  - Operator can run: kubectl patch deployment <svc> -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"<c>","image":"<prev-image-digest>"}]}}}}'
  - Once rollback proven, update mirror git repo with manifest-snapshot pointing at prev-image and sign that manifest (so future reconciles stay consistent).
- If image was pulled into node caches and causes kernel panics or similar, isolate node pool and cordon/evict workloads.

Terraform module notes (opinionated):
- Module: redwood/private-mirror (manages S3/registry mirror, lifecycle policies, and attestation index)
  inputs (string): artifact_repo_prefix, trust_root_kms_key_id, mirror_region, sync_lambda_image
  outputs (string): mirror_bucket, mirror_registry_endpoint, mirror_artifact_path, mirror_sync_timestamp
- Versioning: bump module major version when changing output names or changing resource addressing. Keep backwards compatibility by adding new outputs with suffix _v2 and deprecate in docs for one release cycle.
- State migration: provide an example migration plan in CHANGELOG.md and a tfstate map for resource renames. Always run a terraform plan with -out and verify before apply in customer environments.

Image signing / attestation specifics:
- Use cosign for signature and a separate in-repo attestation that includes: build-id, git-commit, builder-id, used-secrets(hashes), tests-run (smoke/integration), SBOM digest.
- Store trust root as a KMS-wrapped key; expose public key via the trust bundle included in the airgap bundle.
- Verify signatures in two places: pre-import (operator local script) and runtime (admission controller or Argo plugin). Admission controller can block unsanctioned digests by checking the signature index.

Testing and validation suite (CI-side):
- Unit: chart lint (helm lint + kubeval), image scan (clair/trivy), SBOM generation test.
- Integration: deploy to ephemeral airgap-like cluster (no egress), run smoke tests (auth flows, basic inference path), validate logs for errors.
- Upgrade tests: run canary + rollback in CI using KinD or local kind clusters with Argo mock. This is slower but catches reconciliation edge cases.

Operational runbook snippets (for on-call):
- "Preflight failed during import": run verify-signatures --bundle ./bundle --verbose -> check cosign output -> if sign missing, contact build owner and invalidate the bundle.
- "Canary failing after 8m": create immediate rollback PR to canary branch and ping SRE on-call; cordon affected nodes and scale up previous replica set if necessary.
- "Argo stuck reconciling": check argocd-server logs, compare manifest-snapshot tag in git to what Argo sees (argocd app get <app> -o yaml). If Argo is offline, run offline-sync helper.

Key rotation and long-lived attestation considerations:
- Rotation policy: rotate cosign signing keys annually or on incident. Publish new public key into the trust bundle and sign it with previous key to create a chain-of-trust for a transition period.
- For airgapped customers, provide a transitional bundle with both old and new public keys and instructions for operators to update local trust stores.

Open questions / follow-ups (TODOs):
- Do we require an admission controller for all private-deploy customers or make it optional? Operational cost vs safety tradeoff.
- How do we handle multi-tenant mirrors where multiple customers pull from a shared mirror; need artifact scoping namespacing rules.
- Hardening the offline-sync step: can we provide a signed binary or container for the operator to run instead of ad-hoc scripts?

Appendix: quick reference commands
- Local verification: ./tools/verify-signatures --bundle ./bundle.tgz --trust /etc/redwood/trust-bundle.json
- Force rollback (fast path): kubectl -n <ns> set image deploy/<name> <container>=<prev-image-digest>
- Argo offline sync helper: kubectl -n argocd exec job/offline-sync -- /bin/sync-manifests --tag <snapshot-tag>

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc short and link to the full release automation runbook in Confluence. Convert verification script into a small Go binary that returns structured exit codes (0=pass, 1=soft-fail, 2=hard-fail).
- Coordinate with Security to standardize the attestation schema (we've had multiple formats across teams).

End of draft.
